extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, landowners, community organizations, Tribal members, applicants, and other stakeholders in FERC proceedings (potential commenters and intervenors)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural requirements and best practices for submitting comments, protests, motions to intervene, and other filings in Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) docketed proceedings, including filing methods, required content, service, timeliness, and environmental-review participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to participate / Public participation options
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three ways to become involved in the Commission’s review of this project: you can file comments on the project, you can protest the filing, and you can file a motion to intervene in the proceeding. There is no fee or cost for filing comments or intervening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the distinct procedural paths (comments, protests, interventions) and that each has different legal effects (e.g., only intervenors become parties). Deadlines for these actions are provided elsewhere in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and usefulness of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments may include statements of support or objections, to the project as a whole or specific aspects of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The more specific your comments, the more useful they will be. Persons who comment on the environmental review will be placed on the Commission’s environmental mailing list and notified when environmental documents are issued and of meetings associated with the environmental review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protests — eligibility and regulatory compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to sections 157.10(a)(4) and 385.211 of the Commission’s regulations under the NGA, any person may file a protest to the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests must comply with the requirements specified in section 385.2001 of the Commission’s regulations. A protest may also serve as a motion to intervene so long as the protestor states it also seeks to be an intervenor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to intervene — required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to intervene must state, to the extent known, your position regarding the proceeding, as well as your interest in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For an individual, this could include status as a landowner, ratepayer, resident of an impacted community, or recreationist. You do not need to have property directly impacted to intervene. Refer to Rule 214 for additional requirements and guidance (18 CFR 385.214).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to intervene — timeliness and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The deadline for filing a motion to intervene is 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on [intervention deadline specified in the notice].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All timely, unopposed motions to intervene are automatically granted by operation of Rule 214(c)(1). Motions to intervene filed after the deadline are untimely and may be denied; any late-filed motion must show good cause for being late and explain why the time limitation should be waived with justification by reference to factors in Rule 214(d). The applicant has 15 days from submittal of a motion to intervene to file a written objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing methods — eComment, eFiling, and paper filing
rubrics_metrics.description: You may file comments electronically by using the eComment feature (for brief, text-only comments) or by using the eFiling feature (to attach files). You may also file a paper copy by mail or courier to the addresses provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eComment is an easy method for brief, text-only comments. New eFiling users must create an account by clicking on 'eRegister' and be asked to select the type of filing (e.g., 'General' then 'Comment on a Filing' or 'Intervention'). The Commission encourages electronic filing and provides eFiling staff assistance and contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: eComment character limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters can submit brief comments up to 6,000 characters using the eComment system (without prior registration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For longer submissions or attachments, use eFiling (which allows file attachments). Assistance is available from FERC Online Support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference docket number requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In all instances, please reference the Project docket number (e.g., CP25–299-000) in your submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice repeatedly instructs filers to include the correct docket number (often excluding the last three digits when searching eLibrary). Clear docket identification ensures timely and proper recording of submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing format and heading requirements for specific submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: All filings must (1) bear in all capital letters the title 'COMMENTS,' 'REPLY COMMENTS,' 'RECOMMENDATIONS,' 'TERMS AND CONDITIONS,' or 'PRESCRIPTIONS;' (2) set forth in the heading the name of the applicant and the project number of the application to which the filing responds; (3) furnish the name of the person submitting the filing; and (4) otherwise comply with the requirements of 18 CFR 385.2001 through 385.2005.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All comments, recommendations, terms and conditions or prescriptions must set forth their evidentiary basis and otherwise comply with the requirements of 18 CFR 4.34(b). Each filing must be accompanied by proof of service on all persons listed on the service list in accordance with 18 CFR 4.34(b) and 385.2010.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirements (who to serve and how)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protests and motions to intervene must be served on the applicant by mail or by email (with a link to the document) at the contact information provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any subsequent submissions by an intervenor must be served on the applicant and all other parties to the proceeding. Contact information for parties can be downloaded from the service list at the eService link on FERC Online. Service can be via email with a link to the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becoming a party vs. commenting (party status and rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a comment alone will not serve to make the filer a party to the proceeding. To become a party, you must intervene in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only intervenors have the right to request rehearing of Commission orders issued in the proceeding and to subsequently challenge the Commission’s orders in the U.S. Circuit Courts of Appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of various filings and final amendment deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines for interventions, comments, reply comments, and final amendments are specified in the notice (e.g., Intervention Deadline: 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on June 3, 2025; Filing of Comments: July 12, 2025; Reply Comments: August 26, 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final amendments to the application must be filed with the Commission no later than 30 days from the issuance date of the notice of ready for environmental analysis (or otherwise as specified). The Rules of Practice provide rules for extension if deadlines fall on weekends/holidays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof and content of service for evidentiary filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Each filing must be accompanied by proof of service on all persons listed on the service list prepared by the Commission in this proceeding, in accordance with 18 CFR 4.34(b) and 385.2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an intervenor files documents relating to issues that may affect responsibilities of a resource agency, they must also serve a copy on that resource agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Water quality certification filing requirement for applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must file no later than 60 days following the date of issuance of this notice: (1) a copy of the water quality certification; (2) a copy of the request for certification, including proof of the date on which the certifying agency received the request; or (3) evidence of waiver of water quality certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory filing requirement tied to environmental compliance and licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental review participation and mailing list
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons who comment on the environmental review of this project will be placed on the Commission’s environmental mailing list and will receive notification when the environmental documents (EA or EIS) are issued and will be notified of meetings associated with the Commission’s environmental review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being on the environmental mailing list facilitates receiving notices of key milestones (e.g., issuance of EA/EIS) and meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document access and docket search procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission provides opportunity to view and/or print the contents of the notice and other documents in the proceeding via its Home Page using eLibrary. To access, type the docket number excluding the last three digits in the docket number field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The full text is available on eLibrary in PDF and Microsoft Word format. eSubscription allows automatic email notifications and direct links to documents for specific dockets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing standards citation and regulatory references
rubrics_metrics.description: Filings, interventions, protests, and other submissions must comply with the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, including citations provided throughout (e.g., 18 CFR 157.9; 18 CFR 157.10(a)(4); 18 CFR 284.270(b); 18 CFR 385.2001; 18 CFR 385.211; 18 CFR 385.214; 18 CFR 4.34(b); etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices reference specific regulatory sections as the controlling standards for content, form, timeliness, and rights. Filers should consult those cited regulations for full procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission assistance and support services
rubrics_metrics.description: User assistance is available for eLibrary and the Commission’s website during normal business hours from FERC Online Support and the Public Reference Room. The Commission’s Office of Public Participation (OPP) supports meaningful public engagement and can help members of the public access information and navigate Commission processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact information (phone, TTY, email) is provided for eFiling help, OPP assistance, and Public Reference Room inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special filing instructions for eFiling selection
rubrics_metrics.description: When using eFiling, you will be asked to select the type of filing you are making; first select 'General' and then select the appropriate filing type (e.g., 'Comment on a Filing' or 'Intervention').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The eFiling feature includes a document-less intervention option; guidance and links (e.g., to document-less-intervention.pdf) are provided on the FERC website.
